source.title: Symmetries in human brain language pathways correlate with verbal recall.
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

confidence_rationale: The entry that stops this review becoming a rubber stamp for strict lateralisation. Catani et al. dissect the direct Broca-Wernicke connection (arcuate) with diffusion tensor MRI in a normal population and find lateralisation is HETEROGENEOUS -- extreme leftward in more than half of subjects but bilaterally symmetrical in 17.5% -- and, paradoxically, that the MORE SYMMETRIC individuals are BETTER at remembering words via semantic association. Direction mixed: it supports ARC-146's dorsal/ventral distinction (the arcuate is the dorsal route and it IS the lateralised one) while weakening any reading in which strong left-lateralisation is the optimal or canonical configuration. Confidence 0.70: PNAS, in vivo tractography, but 2007-era DTI in a modest normal sample and a correlational cognitive measure.
failure_signatures: Bilateral symmetry of the dorsal route was associated with BETTER semantic verbal recall. If REE hard-codes a strongly lateralised symbolic route because 'that is how brains do it', it is hard-coding the configuration associated with worse performance on the one cognitive measure this study took -- and the population variation implies lateralisation degree is a PARAMETER, not a constant.

Only 17.5% of subjects were bilaterally symmetric and more than half were extremely leftward: the distribution is wide and possibly multimodal. ARC-146 is written as an architectural commitment (a fact about the design) rather than as a parameter with a distribution, and the biology here is the latter.

The cognitive advantage is specific to semantic-association word recall, which is arguably a VENTRAL-stream-flavoured task. A symmetric DORSAL route correlating with better ventral-flavoured performance is not straightforwardly interpretable, and could reflect a third variable (overall white-matter integrity, sex -- the authors note females were more likely to be symmetric).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Diffusion tensor MRI virtual dissection of language pathways in a normal population showed interhemispheric differences in direct connections between Broca's and Wernicke's territories, with extreme leftward lateralisation in more than half of subjects and bilaterally symmetrical distribution in only 17.5%. Individuals with more symmetric patterns of connections were better overall at remembering words using semantic association, and preliminary analysis suggested females are more likely to have a symmetrical pattern. Bilateral representation, not extreme lateralisation, might ultimately be advantageous for specific cognitive functions.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-146 separates a dorsal structured-symbolic route from an affective-coupling system. Catani et al. confirm that the dorsal route (the direct Broca-Wernicke arcuate connection) is indeed the lateralised one, which supports the separation. But they also show its lateralisation is a population PARAMETER with wide variance rather than an architectural constant, and that the extreme-left configuration is not the high-performing one on semantic recall. For REE this converts 'how lateralised should the symbolic route be' from a fact to be copied into a design variable to be chosen -- and suggests the answer is not 'as lateralised as possible'.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The cognitive advantage found is for semantic-association word recall, which is a ventral-flavoured function, while the anatomical measure is the dorsal arcuate. That cross-stream relationship is not straightforwardly interpretable and could reflect general white-matter integrity or the sex difference the authors themselves flag. The imaging is also 2007-era deterministic DTI, which is known to under-recover crossing fibres and can therefore exaggerate apparent right-hemisphere absence. Read this as evidence that lateralisation is variable and not obviously optimised, not as a quantitative target.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adult human population; in vivo diffusion tensor MRI virtual dissection of perisylvian language pathways with cognitive testing.

confidence_components.notes: PNAS with in vivo tractography and a cognitive correlate; source quality good but capped by 2007 DTI methodology and a modest normal sample. Mapping fidelity moderate -- it speaks to the dorsal route's lateralisation, which ARC-146 assumes rather than asserts quantitatively. Transfer risk moderate; the cross-stream cognitive correlation is the weak joint.
